title: AP CSA Java essentials
examples: When should I use an ArrayList instead of a regular array?
How does inheritance actually save me time in coding?
Can I use classes to model real-world objects better?

explain.say: Today we look at building code with Java classes.
A class is like a blueprint for creating objects in Java.
Next we explore the ArrayList, which is a flexible list structure.
Two dimensional arrays help us model grids or tables of data.
Inheritance allows a new class to adopt features from an existing one.
In real life, think of a vehicle. A Car is a type of Vehicle.

faq.q: Why should I use ArrayList over a standard array?
faq.a: ArrayLists can grow or shrink in size as you add or remove items easily. You might also ask if I can change the size later, or what is the difference between ArrayList and array?
asks: Is ArrayList more flexible than an array?
When do I use ArrayList instead of array?

faq.q: What is the main benefit of inheritance in Java?
faq.a: Inheritance promotes code reuse by letting one class adopt properties from another. You could also ask how do I reuse code, or what is superclass usage?
asks: How does inheritance help with code?
Can I make a new class based on an old one?

faq.q: How do I correctly initialize a 2D array?
faq.a: You must specify the number of rows and the number of columns when declaring it. Another way to ask is how do I set up a grid, or what is the syntax for 2D arrays?
asks: What is the setup for a grid in Java?
How do I declare a matrix?

faq.q: What is the difference between an attribute and a method in a class?
faq.a: Attributes hold data or state, while methods define actions or behaviors the object can perform. You might also ask what is data versus behavior, or what are class variables and functions?
asks: What is the difference between variables and functions in a class?
How do I store data and actions in one class?

faq.q: Can I use inheritance with multiple classes?
faq.a: Java supports single inheritance, meaning a class can only directly inherit from one parent class. You might also ask does Java support multiple inheritance, or what is the limitation of inheritance?
asks: Can a class get traits from two parents?
Is there a limit to what can inherit from what?

facts: A class acts as a blueprint for creating objects.
ArrayList automatically manages its underlying storage size.
In inheritance, the child class gains attributes and methods from the parent.
A 2D array uses two indices: one for the row and one for the column.

quiz.say: If you need a list whose size might change often, which structure is best?
quiz.why: ArrayList is designed to resize dynamically, making it perfect for unknown data counts.

wrong.0: A class is a blueprint, not a container for a collection of items.
wrong.2: Standard arrays have a fixed size set when they are first created.
wrong.3: 2D arrays are specifically for grid-like data, not general lists.

quiz.say: If Class B inherits from Class A, what does Class B automatically get?
quiz.why: Inheritance means the child class receives all the public members of the parent class.

wrong.1: It also receives the behaviors, which are the methods.
wrong.2: It must also gain the data storage, which are the attributes.
wrong.3: It gains the parent's set, not a completely new, unrelated set.

quiz.say: To access the element at the third row and second column of a 2D array, what indices are used?
quiz.why: Arrays use zero-based indexing, so the third row is index two, and the second column is index one.

wrong.0: This skips the correct column index, making it point to the wrong spot.
wrong.2: This assumes counting starts from one, which is incorrect in programming.
wrong.3: This accesses the first row and the third column, mixing up the order.
